{{Short description|Equivalence between the categories of chain complexes and simplicial abelian groups}}
In [[mathematics]], more precisely, in the theory of [[simplicial set]]s, the '''Dold–Kan correspondence''' (named after [[Albrecht Dold]] and [[Daniel Kan]]) states<ref name=":0">{{harvp|Goerss|Jardine|1999|loc=Ch 3. Corollary 2.3}}</ref> that there is an [[equivalence of categories|equivalence]] between the [[category (mathematics)|category]] of (nonnegatively graded) [[chain complex]]es and the category of [[simplicial abelian group]]s. Moreover, under the equivalence, the <math>n</math>th [[homology group]] of a chain complex is the <math>n</math>th [[homotopy group]] of the corresponding simplicial abelian group, and a [[chain homotopy]] corresponds to a [[simplicial homotopy]]. (In fact, the correspondence preserves the respective standard [[model category|model structure]]s.) The correspondence is an example of the nerve and realization paradigm.<ref>{{nLab|id=nerve+and+realization#doldkan_correspondence|title=nerve and realization}}</ref>

There is also an [[∞-category]]-version of the Dold–Kan correspondence.<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=§ 1.2.4.}}</ref> The book "Nonabelian Algebraic Topology"<ref>{{Cite book | last1=Brown | first1=Ronald|author1-link=Ronald Brown (mathematician)| last2=Higgins | first2=Philip J. | last3=Sivera | first3=Rafael |title=Nonabelian Algebraic Topology: filtered spaces, crossed complexes, cubical homotopy groupoids | publisher=[[European Mathematical Society]] | location=Zurich | series=Tracts in Mathematics | isbn= 978-3-03719-083-8 | year=2011 | volume=15}}</ref> has a Section 14.8 on [[cubical set|cubical]] versions of the Dold–Kan theorem, and relates them to a previous equivalence of categories between cubical omega-groupoids and crossed complexes, which is fundamental to the work of that book.

== Examples ==
For a chain complex ''C'' that has an [[abelian group]] ''A'' in degree ''n'' and zero in all other degrees, the corresponding simplicial group is the [[Eilenberg–MacLane space]] <math>K(A, n)</math>.

== Detailed construction ==
The Dold–Kan correspondence between the category '''sAb''' of simplicial abelian groups and the category <math>\text{Ch}_{\geq 0}(\textbf{Ab})</math> of nonnegatively graded chain complexes can be constructed explicitly through a pair of [[Functor|functors]]<ref name=":0" /><sup>pg 149</sup> so that these functors form an [[equivalence of categories]]. The first functor is the normalized chain complex functor
<blockquote><math>
N\colon s\textbf{Ab} \to \text{Ch}_{\geq 0}(\textbf{Ab})
</math></blockquote>
and the second functor is the "simplicialization" functor
<blockquote><math>
\Gamma\colon \text{Ch}_{\geq 0}(\textbf{Ab}) \to s\textbf{Ab}
</math></blockquote>
constructing a simplicial abelian group from a chain complex. The formed equivalence is an instance of a special type of adjunction, called the '''nerve-realization paradigm'''<ref>{{cite book |last=Loregian |first=Fosco |title=(Co)end Calculus |chapter= |year=2021 |page=85 |publisher=
[[Cambridge University Press]]|series=London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series |volume=468|doi=10.1017/9781108778657 |arxiv=1501.02503 |isbn=978-1-108-77865-7 }}</ref> (also called a '''nerve-realization context''') where the data of this adjunction is determined by what's called a cosimplicial object<ref>{{nLab|id=cosimplicial+object|title=cosimplicial object}}</ref> <math>dk\colon \Delta \to \text{Ch}_{\geq 0}(\textbf{Ab})</math>, and the adjunction then takes the form
<blockquote><math>
\Gamma = \mathrm{Lan}_y dk : \text{Ch}_{\geq 0}(\textbf{Ab}) \dashv s\textbf{Ab} : \mathrm{Lan}_{dk} y = N
</math></blockquote>
where we take the left [[Kan extension]] and <math>y</math> is the [[Yoneda_lemma#The_Yoneda_embedding|Yoneda embedding]].

=== Normalized chain complex ===
Given a simplicial abelian group <math>A_\bullet \in \text{Ob}(\text{s}\textbf{Ab})</math> there is a chain complex <math>NA_\bullet</math> called the '''normalized chain complex''' (also called the '''Moore complex''') with terms
<blockquote><math>
NA_n = \bigcap^{n-1}_{i=0}\ker(d_i) \subset A_n
</math></blockquote>
and differentials given by
<blockquote><math>
NA_n \xrightarrow{(-1)^nd_n} NA_{n-1}
</math></blockquote>
These differentials are well defined because of the [[Simplicial set|simplicial identity]]
<blockquote><math>
d_i \circ d_n = d_{n-1}\circ d_i : A_n \to A_{n-2}
</math></blockquote>
showing the image of <math>d_n \colon NA_n \to A_{n-1}</math> is in the kernel of each <math>d_i\colon NA_{n-1} \to NA_{n-2}</math>. This is because the definition of <math>NA_n</math> gives <math>d_i(NA_n) = 0</math>.

Now, composing these differentials gives a commutative diagram
<blockquote><math>
NA_n \xrightarrow{(-1)^nd_n} NA_{n-1} \xrightarrow{(-1)^{n-1}d_{n-1}} NA_{n-2}
</math></blockquote>
and the composition map <math>(-1)^n(-1)^{n-1}d_{n-1}\circ d_n</math>. This composition is the zero map because of the [[Simplicial set|simplicial identity]]
<blockquote><math>
d_{n-1}\circ d_n = d_{n-1}\circ d_{n-1}
</math></blockquote>
and the inclusion <math>\text{Im}(d_n) \subset NA_{n-1}</math>, hence the normalized chain complex is a chain complex in <math>\text{Ch}_{\geq 0 }(\textbf{Ab})</math>. Because a simplicial abelian group is a functor
<blockquote><math>
A_\bullet \colon \text{Ord} \to \textbf{Ab}
</math></blockquote>
and morphisms <math>A_\bullet \to B_\bullet</math> are given by natural transformations, meaning the maps of the simplicial identities still hold, the normalized chain complex construction is functorial.
